waivers.reason: Push+SiftUp (the insert path) and Peek/Pop+SiftDown+HighestPriorityChild (the remove/inspect path) share only the backing HeapArray, which check-class-size's own majority-connector filter deliberately treats as plumbing rather than a distinguishing responsibility (see cluster_judgment.go's cross_Cutting_Connectors comment) - but for a heap, that shared backing store is the entire reason both paths belong to one type. Splitting insert from remove into separate classes over one array would fragment an inherently unified abstraction, not clarify it.

the metric's majority-connector filter excludes _items/_head/Count as plumbing (every method touches at least one), then clusters the survivors by which private helper they happen to call (BackIndex vs EnsureCapacity) - producing a 'front vs back' split that is not a real responsibility boundary for a single wraparound buffer. GetFront/RemoveFront read/write the same _head-relative slots AddFront/RemoveBack do; splitting front-end and back-end operations into separate types would duplicate the wraparound arithmetic, not separate concerns.

the parent-array accessors (GetParent/SetParent) and rank-array accessors (GetRank/IncrementRank) cluster separately because the metric excludes the ValidateId call they all share as a majority connector - but parent and rank are two facets of one disjoint-set forest's per-id state, not two responsibilities; DisjointSet.Union already needs both together for every link decision, so splitting them would just make the caller hold two collaborators instead of one.

check-function-cohesion's own doc calls this rule advisory: 'two clusters over different locals may still be one idea, and extraction has a cost that can outweigh the gain.' Each flagged test performs one action (a push/add/union/etc.) and then asserts several independent postconditions of it (Count, the stored value, a second collection's state); the assertions share no local with each other because each reads a different facet of the same mutation, not because the test does two unrelated things. Splitting one assertion per helper function would fragment a single, small, readable test for no reader benefit.
